articles.title: George Eliot, writer: "It is never too late to be what you might have been"
articles.standfirst: George Eliot and the mystery of an enduring quote
articles.summary: George Eliot and the mystery of an enduring quote
articles.body:
The words “It is never too late to be what you might have been” are among the most recognizable quotations associated with George Eliot .

Yet there’s an important problem with the attribution: researchers haven’t found the sentence in Eliot’s novels, letters, or other known writings.

Quote Investigator traces the earliest known appearance of the wording to an 1881 issue of Literary News, where it was submitted by a reader as part of a collection of supposed “gems” from Eliot . The quotation was printed without a source, and there’s no evidence that Eliot actually wrote or said it.

That mystery is interesting because the sentiment fits Eliot’s reputation as a writer concerned with moral choices and experience.

Born Mary Ann Evans in Warwickshire in 1819, she later moved to London, worked at the Westminster Review and became an intellectual before turning to fiction. She adopted the name George Eliot when her first novel, Adam Bede, appeared in 1859.

Her novels rejected romantic conventions and focused on ordinary people, relationships and difficult social realities. Works including The Mill on the Floss, Silas Marner and Middlemarch established her as a novelist of the Victorian era.

The novelist behind the famous words

Middlemarch, published in installments during 1871 and 1872, is an example of Eliot’s interest in ambition and unrealized potential. Its physician, Tertius Lydgate, is portrayed as an educated reformer determined to modernize medical practice.

Eliot’s own life involved choices that challenged Victorian expectations. Her long partnership with philosopher and critic George Henry Lewes defied social rules, while her career demonstrated how far she could move beyond the world in which she was raised. After Lewes died in 1878, she married John Cross in 1880, but died that year at age 61.

The famous quotation, then, may not belong to George Eliot . Quote Investigator suggests it may have evolved from Adelaide Anne Procter’s 1859 poem “A Legend of Provence,” which includes the line, “We always may be what we might have been.”

Even if the wording isn’t Eliot’s , the words reflect a question that runs through her fiction over how much of a life is shaped by choices and circumstances.

articles.title: Virginia Woolf, writer: "If you do not tell the truth about yourself, you cannot tell it about other people"
articles.standfirst: The British writer advocates honesty and self-knowledge as key tools
articles.summary: The British writer advocates honesty and self-knowledge as key tools
articles.body:
The human being is full of mistakes and moments that lead them to analyze their own actions in depth . This is a requirement in order to, over time, grow and move toward a more honest path of self-care and self-knowledge that helps maintain coherence, identity, and go through life without filters or masks that hide the truth about oneself.

Virginia Woolf , one of the most celebrated British writers of all time, is one of the people who most strongly defends this idea, and proof of this is her famous quote: “If you do not tell the truth about yourself, you cannot tell it about other people” .

The need not to deceive oneself

This reflection has several aspects to take into account, beginning with the need to ‘lay bare’ your own soul before yourself . Knowing and accepting your own fears, weaknesses, and strengths helps you be more truthful and allows you to portray the human condition better. This, according to Woolf, is very important in a writer's work.

Another relevant point is that, according to the British writer's phrase, no one can express criticism or judgment about someone unless they have first done so about themselves . If one does not examine, accept, and know their own mistakes, something that in any case makes us human, they are disqualified from expressing them about others in a legitimate way.

Likewise, Woolf maintains that masks in front of society are not compatible with a writer , since only someone who goes without filters or walls and shows themselves as they are can and has the ability to see the reality of others. Thus, looking inward before speaking about others is essential, since empathy is born from this and allows reality to be described more faithfully through literature.

articles.title: Thomas Hobbes, philosopher: "Curiosity is the lust of the mind"
articles.standfirst: Hobbes's social contract theory can help us understand the legitimacy of our governments
articles.summary: Hobbes's social contract theory can help us understand the legitimacy of our governments
articles.body:
The relentless pursuit of happiness and the fear of loneliness are essential dilemmas that we face throughout our existence. Hobbes’s phrase , which suggests that curiosity is a form of mental lust , highlights the contemporary unease about our inability to find satisfaction in the present. The need for approval and the constant fear of making mistake s fuel our frustration and divert us from our path toward a fulfilling life.

In a world where the future seems uncertain, many feel lost and distressed. The work " Leviathan " reflects how these universal problems affect our human nature, portraying a cycle of dissatisfaction that leads us to constantly desire more, without being able to enjoy the present.

To understand the problem of the legitimacy of government and the obligation of citizens, the thought of Thomas Hobbes offers a particularly interesting perspective. His reflection on the social contract proposes that individuals give up certain freedoms in exchange for protection and order through an implicit agreement that justifies governmental authority.

“Curiosity is the lust of the mind”

The theory of the social contract in Thomas Hobbes's thought

Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679) was an English philosopher notable for being one of the founders of modern political philosophy. His most influential work, " Leviathan ", lays the foundations of social contract theory and addresses topics such as political absolutism and the legitimacy of power. In a context of political instability and civil war, Hobbes reflected on the need for a strong government that would guarantee security and social order.

Hobbes's thought centers on the idea that, in its natural state, human beings live in constant chaos, a "war of all against all." This state of nature, according to him, requires the creation of a social contract in which individuals give up certain freedoms in exchange for protection and stability. His ideas are interrelated with those of philosophers such as John Locke, who, although he also deals with the social contract, defends a more optimistic view of human nature and individual rights, contrasting with Hobbes's pessimism.

One of his most famous phrases, "Curiosity is the lust of the mind" , reflects his view of human desires as drivers of behavior. For Hobbes, curiosity, as an uncontrollable desire, can lead to dissatisfaction and the transformation of individuals into destructive beings. This ties in with his idea that regulation and social control are necessary to prevent our impulses from generating chaos and disorder in everyday life.

The phrase "Curiosity is the lust of the mind" is still relevant today, since in daily life in the 21st century, where access to information is almost unlimited, we can observe the effects of this unbridled curiosity. Social media, the constant search for novelty, and information overload create a scenario in which mental and emotional disorder can prevail. The need to establish limits and a sense of order in our pursuit of knowledge and experiences is a reflection that Hobbes anticipated in his analysis of human psychology and politics.

The theory of the social contract in Thomas Hobbes's thought

Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679) was an English philosopher notable for being one of the founders of modern political philosophy. His most influential work, " Leviathan ", lays the foundations of social contract theory and addresses topics such as political absolutism and the legitimacy of power. In a context of political instability and civil war, Hobbes reflected on the need for a strong government that would guarantee security and social order.

Hobbes's thought centers on the idea that, in its natural state, human beings live in constant chaos, a "war of all against all." This state of nature, according to him, requires the creation of a social contract in which individuals give up certain freedoms in exchange for protection and stability. His ideas are interrelated with those of philosophers such as John Locke, who, although he also deals with the social contract, defends a more optimistic view of human nature and individual rights, contrasting with Hobbes's pessimism.

One of his most famous phrases, "Curiosity is the lust of the mind" , reflects his view of human desires as drivers of behavior. For Hobbes, curiosity, as an uncontrollable desire, can lead to dissatisfaction and the transformation of individuals into destructive beings. This ties in with his idea that regulation and social control are necessary to prevent our impulses from generating chaos and disorder in everyday life.

The phrase "Curiosity is the lust of the mind" is still relevant today, since in daily life in the 21st century, where access to information is almost unlimited, we can observe the effects of this unbridled curiosity. Social media, the constant search for novelty, and information overload create a scenario in which mental and emotional disorder can prevail. The need to establish limits and a sense of order in our pursuit of knowledge and experiences is a reflection that Hobbes anticipated in his analysis of human psychology and politics.

articles.title: Astronomers detect radio signals directly from an exoplanet for the first time
articles.standfirst: The research has focused on the Beta Pictoris star system
articles.summary: The research has focused on the Beta Pictoris star system
articles.body:
Knowing whether we are alone in the Universe or not is one of the unknowns that generates the most uncertainty among both astronomers and the global population. In search of resolving this question, a team from the Harvard & Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics and the University of Oregon has announced that it has received a radio signal coming from an exoplanet (a planet outside the Solar System), as reported by the outlet ScienceAlert.

Previously, it was not possible to pinpoint with complete precision the radio signals detected in systems that host planets to the planets themselves, but rather to the stars they orbit around . Now, however, the exoplanet from which the signal originates has been identified .

However, this is not about aliens trying to make contact with Earth . It is a signal coming from the exoplanet's aurora, which is created from charged particles that interact with the conditions of atmospheric and magnetic fields to release energy . Earth itself also has auroras, which appear as the northern and southern lights.

The researchers explain in the study that “although auroral radio bursts are observed on Solar System planets and on some ultracool dwarf planets, until now no radio detection had been unequivocally localized to an extrasolar planet rather than to its host star .”

For the first time the signal comes from an exoplanet and not from a star

“ We detected rapid, recurrent bursts with high circular polarization , as well as persistent emissions, at frequencies from 0.85 to 3.5 GHz. ,” the scientists note. The radio frequencies were observed through the MeerKAT array of radio telescopes, located in South Africa.

On this occasion, the focus of attention was the Beta Pictoris system , located 63.4 light-years away from our planet and made up of the star that gives it its name and three planets orbiting around it: Beta Pictoris b, Beta Pictoris c, and Beta Pictoris d . Using the superbright galactic cores called quasars as a reference, the researchers determined that it was planet b, and not the star, that sent the signal .

“ No known physical mechanism that causes radio emission in early-type stars can explain the observed emission ,” they state. The theory is that Beta Pictoris b has a strong magnetic field . “This constitutes the first direct measurement of the magnetic field strength of an exoplanet, and is consistent with dynamo scaling predictions (the internal processes that generate the magnetic field) for a young and massive giant planet ,” they emphasize.

articles.title: The Real Reason Winter Hats Have Pom-Poms Exploded Online—And It’s Not for Fashion
articles.standfirst: This is the real reason for this eye-catching object
articles.summary: This is the real reason for this eye-catching object
articles.body:
There are details that are part of people’s daily lives and we never stop to wonder why they are there, how they were made, or when it was first done . One of them is the wool pom-pom found on many hats worn during the winter , and which is a classic in situations such as, for example, trips to the snow. Now, this addition has a purpose, and it has recently been discovered .

The truth is that its function is not simply aesthetic , as had been taken for granted for decades. For example, on sailors' hats it was common to see a red pom-pom, and its presence was mainly due to safety reasons. Apparently, the cabins and corridors were narrow and, as a result, sailors often hit their heads . This simple detail on their hats was able to cushion those impacts.

All the functions of the wool pom-pom on hats

At times, the pompom was used as a distinction among the various affiliations or ranks . Meanwhile, these classic wool pompoms worn in winter are not simple hat decorations, which serve as insulation against the cold for our heads. These details also do their job in terms of protection .

These pom-poms help retain heat at the top of the head and, because of their compact shape, act as an additional barrier and prevent the cold from getting in fully. Proof of this is that this type of hat with pom-poms is very common in those countries with the harshest winters.

Likewise, the pom-pom serves other functions when practicing a sport, since during a blizzard or during a march, pom-poms are much easier to distinguish than the hat , which makes it possible to spot someone from a certain distance.

articles.title: After 95 years, Adolf Hitler's alibi does not hold up: they suspect he may have participated in the murder of his niece
articles.standfirst: The documents found in the Munich archives cast doubt on where he was when this crime occurred
articles.summary: The documents found in the Munich archives cast doubt on where he was when this crime occurred
articles.body:
Almost a century later, historical research has called into question Adolf Hitler's official alibi regarding the death of his niece, Geli Raubal . In September 1931, the 23-year-old woman was found dead from a gunshot in the Munich apartment of the Nazi leader, with whom she lived. Although the official version classified the incident as a suicide, the press and the political opposition of the time immediately questioned that account , suspecting that the future dictator may have been involved in the tragic outcome.

'The controversy has resurfaced following the discovery of valuable documents in the Munich archives by historian Harald Sandner , as revealed by the magazine "Der Spiegel". Sandner has located two death notices and a death certificate in the civil registry dating the discovery of the body to the morning of September 18, 1931, at 10:15 a.m. This information contradicts the version maintained by Hitler , who claimed to have left the city a day earlier to avoid any link to the tragic event.'

A leaky alibi... almost a century later

The official account that exonerated the leader was based on a police report written on September 28, ten days after the death. The temporal inconsistency suggests possible manipulation to protect Hitler's public image . As historian Thomas Weber explains, the Nazi leader needed to present himself as a model of moral virtue in his rise to power, a claim that would have been destroyed if he had been directly associated with the death of his young relative.

Added to the doubts about his whereabouts is the fact that the authorities of the time never ordered an autopsy to be performed on Raubal's body . Although these documentary findings do not constitute definitive proof of homicide, they do reinforce the hypotheses circulating at the time about Hitler's responsibility. Various newspapers then suggested that the politician may have ended his niece's life or ordered her murder in order to maintain strict control over her actions.

The background of the conflict appears to have been a violent argument prior to the death. Multiple testimonies indicate that the reason for the dispute was Hitler's refusal to allow the young woman to move to Vienna to continue her singing studies . Ninety-five years later, these new clues rekindle suspicions about one of the darkest and most covered-up episodes in the dictator's personal circle.

articles.title: Miss Jamaica sues Miss Universe following a life-altering brain injury: Who is Gabrielle Henry?
articles.standfirst: Inside the devastating fall that changed Gabrielle Henry's life forever
articles.summary: Inside the devastating fall that changed Gabrielle Henry's life forever
articles.body:
Former Miss Jamaica Gabrielle Henry has filed a lawsuit against the Miss Universe Organization nearly a year after a devastating stage accident in Thailand left her with serious brain injuries and dramatically disrupted her medical career.

Henry , a Jamaican doctor and former beauty queen, filed the lawsuit on September 21, 2026, in Delaware Superior Court. She is suing the Miss Universe Organization, JKN Legacy Inc. and Legacy Holding Group USA over the November 2025 incident.

The complaint includes allegations of negligence, premises liability, negligent hiring and supervision, and emotional distress.

The case stems from November 19, 2025, when Henry was competing in the preliminary evening gown portion of the 74th Miss Universe competition in Bangkok, Thailand. According to her lawsuit, she was following rehearsed instructions when she was directed to turn toward the left side of the stage.

Henry alleges that intense stage lighting impaired her visibility before she suddenly fell approximately five feet through an opening in the stage. The complaint describes the opening as unmarked and uncovered, with lighting equipment and concrete below it.

“I fell into an unguarded hole, sustaining a traumatic brain injury that permanently altered the course of my life. All at once, a beautiful moment became a shattered dream,” Henry wrote in an essay published by People.

The fall left H e nry unconscious and resulted in a traumatic brain injury, including acute subarachnoid hemorrhage, a frontal lobe hemorrhagic contusion and a subdural hemorrhage.

She was hospitalized in Thailand from November 19 until December 10, 2025, according to reports based on the lawsuit.

Gabrielle Henry’s life after the accident

The consequences extended far beyond the end of Henry’s pageant journey. At the time of the accident, she was pursuing an ophthalmology residency.

Her injuries have prevented her from returning to her medical training in the same way, and she says she continues to deal with neurological and cognitive symptoms requiring medical care and rehabilitation.

Henry has described the accident as a life-changing experience. She said she had no memory of the actual fall and recalled waking to see her mother beside her in the hospital. She also said she believes the accident could have been prevented if appropriate safety measures had been in place.

Her lawsuit alleges that concerns about the staging and lighting had been raised before the accident. It also claims that changes were made to the stage after her fall, including additional lighting around its edges.

The Miss Universe Organization has offered a different account. In a statement reported by Jamaican media, the organization said it hadn't been served with the lawsuit and therefore couldn't comment on allegations it hadn't reviewed.

It also said Miss Grand International and Miss Universe Thailand were responsible for the event's production, venue, stage and on-site safety. The organization said it paid Henry's hospital expenses and later covered treatment in Jamaica.

Miss Grand International has also disputed Henry's account, saying she may have missed her blocking and wasn't looking toward the runway, while denying that anyone blamed her for the accident. Henry's legal action will now put the competing accounts and responsibility for the stage conditions before the court.

articles.title: The Earth has begun to break apart beneath the Pacific: scientists detect a tectonic phenomenon never seen before
articles.standfirst: The Earth has begun to break apart beneath the Pacific: scientists detect a tectonic phenomenon never seen before
articles.summary: The Earth has begun to break apart beneath the Pacific: scientists detect a tectonic phenomenon never seen before
articles.body:
A team of scientists from Louisiana State University has observed for the first time in great detail how a subduction zone is beginning to break apart beneath the Pacific Northwest . The finding, published by Science Daily, shows that these gigantic tectonic systems could disappear gradually , breaking apart piece by piece, instead of stopping suddenly.

The research focuses on the Cascadia subduction zone, off Vancouver Island , where the Juan de Fuca and Explorer plates slowly slide beneath the North American plate . These regions are responsible for some of the most powerful earthquakes and volcanic eruptions on the planet .

The researchers combined earthquake records with images obtained using seismic reflection techniques. During the CASIE21 experiment, funded by the National Science Foundation in 2021, a ship sent sound waves toward the seafloor and a 15-kilometer underwater cable recorded the echoes. The procedure made it possible to obtain detailed images of the structures hidden beneath the ocean depths.

Fractures can reach 75 kilometers and displace the plates by five kilometers

The results revealed numerous fractures in the sinking plate. One of them extends for about 75 kilometers and shows a displacement of approximately five kilometers . Some areas of this fracture are still recording earthquakes, while others remain unusually quiet, which could indicate that certain fragments have already separated.

According to the authors, the process would be creating small independent plates , known as microplates. The so-called transform faults, where blocks of the crust move laterally , would act like a kind of geological scissors that promotes fragmentation.

Each rupture can last for millions of years . However, as the fragments break away, the plate loses some of the strength that keeps subduction active.

The discovery could also help explain geological problems and remnants of ancient plates , such as the fragments associated with the vanished Farallon Plate, and provide new clues about the planet's tectonic evolution.

articles.title: Who is Maricarmen, the woman who mobilized thousands in Spain and prompted Antonio Banderas to speak out
articles.standfirst: María del Carmen Abascal lived for more than 70 years in the same apartment in Madrid until she was evicted and had to leave her home on a stretcher.
articles.summary: María del Carmen Abascal lived for more than 70 years in the same apartment in Madrid until she was evicted and had to leave her home on a stretcher.
articles.body:
Until just a few days ago, Maricarmen was virtually unknown outside her neighborhood in Madrid . At 87 years old, she led a life away from the spotlight in an apartment on Alcalde Sainz de Baranda Street, in the Retiro district, where she had lived for more than seven decades.

Everything changed on September 23. María del Carmen Abascal was evicted from that home and left the building on a stretcher before being taken by ambulance to Gregorio Marañón Hospital. The scene spread across Spain and turned a complicated dispute over an old rental contract into a story with a name and a face.

The house in which Maricarmen spent practically her entire life is the protagonist of this story. Her relationship with that home dates back to 1956, when her father signed the lease agreement. There Maricarmen lived with her parents, saw her relatives die, and remained for approximately seven decades.

And here appears one of the most particular aspects of the story: the origin of the contract and the rules of the Franco era ended up having consequences many decades later.

The original contract was signed by her father. According to the reconstruction by El País, her mother could not appear as the holder under the same conditions due to the legal restrictions that at the time affected women. When the father died, the contract passed to the mother; when she died in 2005, Maricarmen was subrogated into it .

Over the years, the property ended up in the hands of Urbagestión Desarrollo e Inversión, which acquired the home in 2018. The conflict that would ultimately force the elderly woman out of her house did not arise from non-payment: she continued paying the rent. The battle was legal and centered on whether that second subrogation could remain valid.

So, why could she be evicted if she was paying the rent?

This point is fundamental because the conflict did not arise simply because Maricarmen stopped paying. The problem was legal: the property owner maintained that the old contract should already have expired .

The case ended up reaching the Supreme Court , and after years of appeals it upheld the interpretation of the property ownership. The regulations allowed that second subrogation to be extended in certain circumstances, including when the beneficiary had a recognized disability of more than 65%. Maricarmen had a recognized disability of 50%, so she was left out of that exception.

After several attempted evictions and years of legal battle, the eviction was finally carried out on September 23. Maricarmen left the home where she had spent 71 years on a stretcher. That image achieved something that no explanation about contracts, subrogations, or laws had managed until then: to transform her individual case into a story capable of provoking a national reaction.

"Not one more Maricarmen": her name becomes a symbol

Thousands of people took part in housing protests, and Maricarmen ended up becoming one of the symbols of the debate about evictions and rent in Spain.

The impact also reached national politics, where her case was cited while the Government and its partners resumed negotiations on new housing measures.

Maricarmen ceased to be just the name of a tenant. "A Maricarmen" began to be used in the discourse of housing movements as a representation of people who can lose a long-term rental even if they have kept up with their payments.

A virtually unknown retiree became, in a matter of days, a much bigger issue than her own story. Her name appeared on banners and in slogans, and the mobilization continued even after a possible solution for her particular case became known.

On September 23, 2026, the eviction was finally carried out after several previous attempts.

Neighbors and activists had been mobilizing for some time to prevent it . On the day of the eviction, hundreds of people showed up. Maricarmen, who has reduced mobility, ended up leaving her home on a stretcher and being transferred by ambulance to Gregorio Marañón Hospital.

Instead of limiting her statements to getting her own home back, she began to speak about others. After the eviction she said:

"I have not managed to defend my home, but I have fought so that others learn to fight for theirs".

Antonio Banderas enters the debate over Maricarmen

The magnitude the case reached became even clearer when Antonio Banderas decided to speak publicly about Maricarmen .

The actor referred this Monday to the eviction during an interview on Herrera en COPE Más Málaga, although he wanted to broaden the focus to all the people going through similar situations.

"I think about this woman, Maricarmen, but I also think about the 25,000 evicted people there have been this year in our country," Banderas said. His reflection did not question the retired woman's situation—he expressed his solidarity with her—but rather the enormous attention focused on a single case compared with other housing-related problems that receive much less exposure.

The actor was even more direct when referring to the political dimension the story had taken on: "I am interested in everything, the whole of reality, not a specific reality for a specific political use" . For Banderas, Maricarmen had become a public symbol, but her case should also serve to look toward other people facing situations related to the loss of their homes.

The unexpected final twist: Maricarmen will be able to return home

And when that image of Maricarmen leaving the building on a stretcher seemed to have written the ending, a twist arrived that would have been hard to imagine five days earlier.

Urbagestión and its representatives reached an agreement so that she can return to the same home from which she was evicted. The Municipal Housing and Land Company of Madrid acted as mediator in a meeting lasting more than four hours, in which the Tenants' Union also took part.

The new contract will last for eight years and the rent will not exceed 30% of her net income, an amount that her lawyer estimated to be similar to the approximately 500 euros she had been paying in rent and other expenses. When the agreement became known, Maricarmen was still hospitalized, although she had already accepted the agreemen t and it is expected that she will return home when she is medically discharged.

In less than a week, María del Carmen Abascal's life changed completely: she left on a stretcher from the home where she had spent more than 70 years, saw her name appear in demonstrations and in the political debate, made it as far as Antonio Banderas's statements and, finally, secured the possibility of returning to the same apartment.

Maricarmen was not famous. Nor was she trying to be. But at 87, her name ended up becoming one of the symbols of the debate over housing in Spain.

Maricarmen ceased to be just the name of a tenant. "A Maricarmen" began to be used in the discourse of housing movements as a representation of people who can lose a long-term rental even if they have kept up with their payments.

A virtually unknown retiree became, in a matter of days, a much bigger issue than her own story. Her name appeared on banners and in slogans, and the mobilization continued even after a possible solution for her particular case became known.
On September 23, 2026, the eviction was finally carried out after several previous attempts.

Neighbors and activists had been mobilizing for some time to prevent it . On the day of the eviction, hundreds of people showed up. Maricarmen, who has reduced mobility, ended up leaving her home on a stretcher and being transferred by ambulance to Gregorio Marañón Hospital.
Instead of limiting her statements to getting her own home back, she began to speak about others. After the eviction she said:
"I have not managed to defend my home, but I have fought so that others learn to fight for theirs".
Antonio Banderas enters the debate over Maricarmen
The magnitude the case reached became even clearer when Antonio Banderas decided to speak publicly about Maricarmen .
The actor referred this Monday to the eviction during an interview on Herrera en COPE Más Málaga, although he wanted to broaden the focus to all the people going through similar situations.

"I think about this woman, Maricarmen, but I also think about the 25,000 evicted people there have been this year in our country," Banderas said. His reflection did not question the retired woman's situation—he expressed his solidarity with her—but rather the enormous attention focused on a single case compared with other housing-related problems that receive much less exposure.

The actor was even more direct when referring to the political dimension the story had taken on: "I am interested in everything, the whole of reality, not a specific reality for a specific political use" . For Banderas, Maricarmen had become a public symbol, but her case should also serve to look toward other people facing situations related to the loss of their homes.
The unexpected final twist: Maricarmen will be able to return home
And when that image of Maricarmen leaving the building on a stretcher seemed to have written the ending, a twist arrived that would have been hard to imagine five days earlier.

Urbagestión and its representatives reached an agreement so that she can return to the same home from which she was evicted. The Municipal Housing and Land Company of Madrid acted as mediator in a meeting lasting more than four hours, in which the Tenants' Union also took part.

The new contract will last for eight years and the rent will not exceed 30% of her net income, an amount that her lawyer estimated to be similar to the approximately 500 euros she had been paying in rent and other expenses. When the agreement became known, Maricarmen was still hospitalized, although she had already accepted the agreemen t and it is expected that she will return home when she is medically discharged.

In less than a week, María del Carmen Abascal's life changed completely: she left on a stretcher from the home where she had spent more than 70 years, saw her name appear in demonstrations and in the political debate, made it as far as Antonio Banderas's statements and, finally, secured the possibility of returning to the same apartment.
Maricarmen was not famous. Nor was she trying to be. But at 87, her name ended up becoming one of the symbols of the debate over housing in Spain.

articles.title: Attempted hijacking alert: pilot stabs another mid-flight, forcing a FlyDubai plane to divert to Saudi Arabia
articles.standfirst: The aircraft was operating the route between Dubai and Tel Aviv and was carrying more than 150 people
articles.summary: The aircraft was operating the route between Dubai and Tel Aviv and was carrying more than 150 people
articles.body:
This Wednesday, September 30, an incident occurred mid-flight on FlyDubai when one of its planes, which was operating the route between Dubai and Tel Aviv , had to be diverted and finally landed in Saudi Arabia after an altercation broke out between crew members.

Israeli authorities have confirmed to EFE that the incident took place during the flight and that security agencies are handling what happened. At first, the activation of an emergency signal and the aircraft's movements raised fears that it could be a hijacking , although authorities later pointed to a confrontation between the pilots.

According to reports circulated by Israeli media, one of the pilots allegedly attacked the other with a bladed weapon during the flight. These details are still part of the investigation and have not been officially confirmed in all their aspects.

The aircraft's tracking data also show a very steep descent during the journey. The plane lost several thousand meters of altitude within minutes before activating the emergency signal, a maneuver that helped raise the alarm about what was happening on board.

The plane finally landed in Saudi Arabia

The aircraft was diverted to Saudi Arabia and ended up landing at Tabuk airport. The situation also triggered a response from the Israeli authorities, who even deployed fighter jets amid the possibility that it was an in-flight emergency.

Israeli airspace was temporarily closed while the incident was being handled and was later reopened once the plane had landed in Saudi territory.

Israeli authorities have indicated that the situation is under control and that the necessary measures are being taken to ensure the passengers' return to Israel.

The company FlyDubai plans to send another plane to the Saudi airport to transport back to Tel Aviv the passengers who were traveling on the affected aircraft.

The investigation seeks to clarify what happened in the cockpit

The initial data indicate that the origin of the emergency was a confrontation between crew members, although the exact circumstances of the incident still remain to be determined.

A passenger quoted by Israeli media said they had heard screams and seen a violent situation inside the plane. Images have also circulated on social media showing people with blood stains , although the origin of those images and the specific circumstances in which they were taken are still being investigated.

Among the hypotheses being considered is the possibility that one of the pilots may have tried to take control of the plane with the intention of causing an accident . According to this version, the other pilot would have intervened to prevent it. However, this hypothesis has not been officially confirmed and is part of the lines of inquiry currently being investigated.

The flight was carrying more than 150 people and, for the time being, the Israeli authorities have stated that they are working to ensure that the passengers can return to Israel safely. The priority now is to determine what happened inside the plane and why the emergency situation occurred that forced it to change its route.

articles.title: Pilot is stabbed mid-air as Israel-bound plane plunges 17,000 feet
articles.summary: A flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv became a terrifying mid-air emergency after a violent confrontation erupted inside the cockpit.
articles.body:
A flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv became a terrifying mid-air emergency after a violent confrontation erupted inside the cockpit.

According to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the co-pilot stabbed the captain and attempted to crash flydubai Flight FZ1073.

The aircraft suddenly descended nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds as passengers and a crew member forced their way into the cockpit and restrained the alleged attacker.

Other qualified pilots aboard the plane regained control and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All passengers escaped unharmed, and Saudi authorities arrested the co-pilot. Flydubai confirmed a cockpit altercation but said the cause and motive remain under investigation.

articles.title: WARNING VIDEO: Pilot is stabbed mid-air as Israel-bound plane plunges 17,000 feet
articles.standfirst: A violent cockpit confrontation sent a Flydubai flight into an emergency as passengers feared the worst
articles.summary: A violent cockpit confrontation sent a Flydubai flight into an emergency as passengers feared the worst
articles.body:
Terror unfolded in the air aboard a Flydubai flight traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv after the two pilots became involved in a physical altercation . The aircraft was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where both pilots were hospitalized with injuries after the plane landed safely.

According to Israeli officials , the co-pilot stabbed the pilot and then attempted to take control of the aircraft . Passengers intervened and subdued him while other crew members took over and managed to land the Boeing 737 safely in Saudi Arabia. Flydubai confirmed that the aircraft had experienced an incident but said the reasons behind it remained unknown , urging against premature speculation while the investigation continues.

A sudden plunge raised the alarm

Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft rapidly losing altitude during the chaos. Flightradar24 recorded a descent of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the plane sent its first emergency signal. Other flight-tracking data showed the aircraft falling from around 34,000 feet to roughly 16,600 feet in just over two minutes.

The aircraft first transmitted a general emergency signal before sending another alert indicating possible unlawful interference, a code associated with a potential hijacking. The emergency signals triggered a major security response, with Israel scrambling fighter jets as authorities feared the plane could have been hijacked.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said one of the pilots had been arrested and was being questioned after apparently stabbing the other pilot and attempting to crash the plane. The motive behind the confrontation remains unclear, while Saudi authorities continue to investigate what happened aboard the flight.

Passengers faced an unexpected problem on the ground

The emergency landing also created a diplomatic complication after Saudi Arabia rejected an Israeli request to send military aircraft to bring the passengers home. Saudi Arabia does not have diplomatic relations with Israel, so Israeli military planes could not simply arrive to repatriate those on board.

The passengers eventually left Saudi Arabia aboard a replacement Flydubai aircraft after spending eight hours on the ground . Both pilots remained hospitalized after suffering injuries during the incident, while authorities continued working to establish exactly what happened inside the cockpit.

articles.title: Socrates, Greek philosopher: "He is richest who is content with the least, for content is the wealth of nature"
articles.standfirst: More than 2,400 years later, his philosophy still questions whether endless accumulation can ever produce real satisfaction
articles.summary: More than 2,400 years later, his philosophy still questions whether endless accumulation can ever produce real satisfaction
articles.body:
Socrates lived in a city that prized status, influence and public success, yet he became famous for questioning whether any of those things could produce a genuinely good life.

The Athenian philosopher, born around 470 BCE, left no written works of his own. Most of what is known about him comes from figures such as Plato and Xenophon , whose accounts portray a man who lived simply and cared far more about virtue than material comfort.

That philosophy is neatly captured in a line often attributed to Socrates : “He is richest who is content with the least, for content is the wealth of nature.”

The quote doesn't suggest that poverty is desirable or that ambition is pointless. Its deeper challenge is aimed at dependence, and the idea that happiness must constantly be purchased, upgraded or expanded.

Socrates measured wealth by independence

Socrates repeatedly argued that character mattered more than possessions. His life reflected that position. Ancient accounts describe him wearing simple clothing, living modestly and refusing to treat philosophy as a route to financial success.

That independence mattered because it allowed him to question powerful people without needing their approval.

The more a person depends on status, luxury or external validation, the easier it becomes for those things to influence their choices. Socrates ’ version of wealth therefore begins with freedom from unnecessary wants.

Contentment, in that sense, isn't resignation. It's the ability to recognize when enough is genuinely enough, rather than moving endlessly from one desire to another.

That distinction also explains why the quote remains relevant in a culture where comparison is constant. A person can accumulate more money, possessions and recognition while still feeling perpetually behind someone else. Socrates offers a different scoreboard.

Why the least can still mean having more

Someone who is satisfied with what is necessary has access to a form of wealth that cannot easily disappear with a market downturn, job change or loss of social status.

Socrates placed particular value on friendship, knowledge, virtue and the examined life. None of those things can be reduced neatly to a bank balance.

His philosophy ultimately centered on understanding what was truly good rather than simply pursuing what looked desirable. That principle carried enormous consequences.

In 399 BCE, Socrates was sentenced to death after being convicted of impiety and corrupting the youth of Athens, yet he refused to abandon the beliefs that had defined his life.

His enduring influence comes partly from that consistency. And it remains powerful because it challenges one of the most persistent assumptions about success: that having more must always make life better.

Socrates suggested the opposite may sometimes be true. Real wealth, in his view, begins when possessions stop deciding whether a person feels complete.

articles.title: The search for Jesus’ tomb takes a major turn beneath Jerusalem’s Church of the Holy Sepulchre
articles.standfirst: The excavation is providing new information about what existed beneath the church during the period when Jesus lived and died
articles.summary: The excavation is providing new information about what existed beneath the church during the period when Jesus lived and died
articles.body:
The search for the historical setting of Jesus’ death and burial has taken a remarkable turn beneath one of Christianity’s most important sites. Archaeologists excavating beneath Jerusalem’s Church of the Holy Sepulchre have uncovered evidence of an ancient landscape that included a quarry, cultivated areas and funerary activity, features that are consistent with descriptions of the location where the Gospels say Jesus was crucified and buried.

But there is an important distinction between finding evidence that supports the traditional location of Jesus’ tomb and proving that Jesus himself was buried there. The archaeological team, led by Francesca Romana Stasolla of Sapienza University of Rome, has not discovered an inscription identifying Jesus, nor has it recovered physical remains that can be attributed to him. Instead, the excavation is providing new information about what existed beneath the church during the period when Jesus lived and died.

That distinction has not diminished the significance of the discovery. It may, however, change how archaeologists understand the landscape that eventually became the site of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

An excavation hidden beneath one of Christianity’s holiest sites

The archaeological work began as part of a major restoration project. Beginning in 2022, archaeologists from Sapienza University of Rome were allowed to excavate beneath sections of the church floor while restoration and infrastructure work was being carried out. The investigation has continued through multiple campaigns and has involved archaeology, geology, palaeobotany, archaeozoology, material analysis and digital documentation.

The project is unusually complicated because the Church of the Holy Sepulchre remains a functioning place of worship. The archaeological work has been conducted in cooperation with the Christian communities responsible for the sanctuary, including the Greek Orthodox, Catholic and Armenian traditions. Sapienza's 2026 project publication describes the investigation as a multidisciplinary effort examining the church's floors, underground structures and infrastructure.

What began with restoration therefore became something considerably more ambitious: an attempt to reconstruct the history of the ground beneath the church. And the deeper archaeologists went, the more complicated that history became.

A quarry, a garden and ancient graves

According to the excavation findings, the area beneath the church preserves evidence of an ancient quarry that was subsequently reused for agricultural and funerary purposes. The quarry is particularly important because its location fits the historical geography of first- century Jerusalem.

The area now occupied by the Church of the Holy Sepulchre was apparently associated with a quarry and lay outside the city's earlier boundaries during part of the period relevant to Jesus' lifetime. The archaeological record indicates that the landscape subsequently experienced different phases of cultivation, burial and construction.

That matters because the Gospel accounts place Jesus' crucifixion and burial in an area that was outside the city and near a garden. The Gospel of John, for example, describes a garden at the place where Jesus was crucified and says that a new tomb was located there.

The excavations have now provided archaeological evidence that the landscape beneath the later church was not simply an empty stretch of bedrock. It was a changing environment that included quarrying, agriculture and burial.

Evidence of ancient vegetation

Among the most intriguing findings has been evidence of plant life. Archaeobotanical investigations and pollen analysis have identified traces associated with vegetation including olive and grape cultivation. Researchers are using this material to reconstruct how the area was used during antiquity.

For Stasolla , the discovery is particularly interesting because it corresponds with the type of landscape described in the Gospel of John. But archaeologists are careful about what such evidence can establish. Finding evidence of a garden does not prove that the garden described in the Gospel was specifically the garden in which Jesus was buried.

What it does demonstrate is that the environment beneath the church had agricultural use compatible with the broader setting described by the ancient Christian tradition. That is an important archaeological distinction.

articles.title: Who is Hamam al-Hammami, the suspected co-pilot accused of attempting to hijack a Flydubai flight and who violated a ban?
articles.standfirst: Co-pilot in FlyDubai attack is identified
articles.summary: Co-pilot in FlyDubai attack is identified
articles.body:
The co-pilot suspected of stabbing the captain of an Israel-bound FlyDubai flight before passengers and others stopped the attack is an Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami , three people with knowledge of the situation, including a Gulf and a Western diplomat, said.

All spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media. The Gulf diplomat said investigations are underway to establish whether he acted as a “lone wolf or has any connection with any extremist groups.”

The United Arab Emirates said the co-pilot attacked the captain with the cockpit’s crash axe and tried to take control of the plane in a “terrorist attack.”

The co-pilot, who officials said nearly crashed the sharply plummeting flight with 182 people aboard, was barred from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views , a separate person familiar with the matter said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss the ongoing investigation.

The co-pilot was subsequently hired by the United Arab Emirates-based airline , the person said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss the ongoing investigation. It was not immediately clear to what extent he was vetted when he was hired in the Emirates. Oman’s move to bar the co-pilot from flying was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

Wounded captain says he had to get back up to save passengers

The Indian airline captain who helped thwart the apparent attempt to down a flight to Tel Aviv told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that he knew he had to get back on his feet to save everyone on board, after he was stabbed by his co-pilot and the aircraft carrying 182 people plunged into a steep descent.

“I had so many wounds. I had fallen down,” Capt. Smit Machchhar said from a hospital in Abu Dhabi. “I was fighting for my life. At one point I realized that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives.”

Machchhar was seriously injured in Wednesday’s attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker as the Boeing 737 descended sharply , witnesses and Israeli authorities said.

articles.title: Friedrich Nietzsch, philosopher and writer: "I know of no better life purpose than to perish in attempting the great and impossible"
articles.standfirst: A powerful Nietzsche quotation about pursuing ambitious goals has endured
articles.summary: A powerful Nietzsche quotation about pursuing ambitious goals has endured
articles.body:
F riedrich Nietzsche remains one of the most widely discussed philosophers of the modern era, and few ideas associated with his work are as striking as his call to pursue ambitions that appear almost impossible.

The quotation, commonly attributed to Nietzsche , reads: “I know of no better life purpose than to perish in attempting the great and impossible.”

It is worth noting that the wording comes from an unpublished note from 1873 rather than one of Nietzsche's major published books.

A version of the passage appears in material associated with his Untimely Meditations, while modern quotation collections such as Goodreads attribute the shorter formulation directly to Nietzsche .

That distinction matters because Nietzsche's surviving notebooks contain material that was never presented by the philosopher as a finished work.

The quotation nevertheless reflects themes that became central to his thinking: purpose, self-creation, ambition and the challenge of living deliberately rather than simply accepting inherited values.

Nietzsche was born in 1844 in Röcken, near Leipzig, and initially pursued classical philology before becoming one of the most influential and controversial philosophers of the 19th century.

He was appointed to a chair in classical philology at the University of Basel when he was only 24, and his intellectual interests eventually expanded far beyond the discipline.

His philosophical project frequently challenged conventional assumptions about morality, religion, culture and the meaning of a worthwhile life.

Rather than offering a simple formula for happiness, Nietzsche explored how people might create values and purposes for themselves.

What Nietzsche meant by pursuing the "great and impossible"

The quotation's language can initially sound like an endorsement of failure or destruction. Its broader context, however, points toward something different: Nietzsche was emphasizing the importance of setting an elevated purpose rather than drifting without a meaningful goal.

In the longer passage, Nietzsche asks the individual to consider why they exist and, if they cannot immediately provide an answer, to establish an "exalted and noble" aim.

The point is not necessarily that a person should literally seek death, but that a life can be organized around a goal so demanding that pursuing it becomes meaningful in itself.

The phrase animae magnae prodigus, which appears alongside the passage, has been translated in scholarly discussions as suggesting someone who is prodigal or lavish with a great soul.

The surrounding material therefore reinforces the idea of committing oneself wholeheartedly to an ambitious purpose.

That interpretation fits with Nietzsche's broader emphasis on life-affirmation. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy describes affirmation as an important element of his philosophy and notes that Nietzsche sought to challenge values he believed restricted human potential while developing alternative values that could support a more expansive approach to life.

The philosopher's emphasis on creating and pursuing demanding goals also helps explain why the quotation continues to circulate outside academic philosophy.

It can be read as an argument against measuring a meaningful life only through easy victories. A goal can matter because of the person it requires someone to become, not simply because it is eventually achieved.

Another quotation supplied alongside the Nietzsche material points toward a related idea of concentration: “The successful warrior is the average man, with laser-like focus.”

However, that line is attributed to Bruce Lee rather than Nietzsche . Goodreads identifies Bruce Lee as the quoted author, although the site also cautions that its community-added quotations are not independently verified.

The two quotations therefore should not be treated as statements from the same philosopher. They can, however, be considered alongside one another as expressions of a broader cultural fascination with determination and concentrated effort.

Nietzsche's words remain especially provocative because they reject the assumption that purpose must come from certainty about the final result. Instead, the passage places emphasis on choosing something sufficiently ambitious to demand commitment.

More than 150 years after Nietzsche wrote the underlying note, that idea continues to resonate. His formulation asks a fundamental question about purpose: if a person is going to devote their life to something, should the goal be merely achievable, or should it be ambitious enough to transform the person pursuing it?

For Nietzsche, the answer was unmistakably in favor of the latter.

articles.title: Who is Alma Mireya de la Rosa? The Mexican reporter run over live on air in Monterrey
articles.standfirst: The moment was broadcast live and caused great concern among viewers
articles.summary: The moment was broadcast live and caused great concern among viewers
articles.body:
A very tense moment was experienced when reporter Alma Mireya de la Rosa and her cameraman Cristo Morales were hit by a vehicle while covering live the effects of the rain in Monterrey, Nuevo León , quickly causing concern in the Gamavisión studio.

The incident occurred while both journalists were documenting the collapse of a wall in the vicinity of Morones Prieto and Pedro Martínez avenues, in the Nuevo Repueblo neighborhood . Unexpectedly, a pickup truck lost control and ended up crashing into them, leaving the reporter and the cameraman injured. The moment was captured by Morales 's own camera, which continued broadcasting, while in the studio the situation caused concern as they realized what had happened.

Accident in Monterrey: pickup truck runs over reporter and cameraman during live broadcast

In the recording, it can be seen how, after a cargo vehicle passes by, an SUV moves along Morones Prieto Avenue and apparently loses control while traveling over the wet pavement. The vehicle skids and changes course until it heads toward the spot where Alma Mireya de la Rosa and Cristo Morales were covering the damage caused by the rains.

The vehicle ended up hitting both journalists, who fell onto the asphalt, while the pickup truck continued on its path until it crashed into the remains of the wall that were still on the roadway. After the accident, emergency personnel arrived to assist the reporters, and they were later taken to a hospital, where they received a medical evaluation.

Reporter and cameraman run over in Monterrey: what is their health condition?

After the accident, Alma Mireya de la Rosa and Cristo Morales were attended to by emergency responders and taken to a hospital for a medical evaluation. According to the initial reports, both journalists suffered various injuries resulting from the impact, although none of them were considered serious, so they remained under medical care to rule out complications.

The accident occurred while the journalists were covering the collapse of a wall caused by the rains on Morones Prieto avenue. The incident was recorded during the live broadcast and took place amid a day marked by flooding, stranded vehicles, and road closures in different parts of Nuevo León.

articles.title: A 75-kilometer fracture reveals that a tectonic plate is splitting apart in the depths of the Pacific
articles.standfirst: The finding allows a close-up look at how an oceanic plate is fragmenting in one of the most tectonically active areas on the planet
articles.summary: The finding allows a close-up look at how an oceanic plate is fragmenting in one of the most tectonically active areas on the planet
articles.body:
A fracture about 75 kilometers long has allowed scientists to gain a new perspective on what is happening in the depths of the Pacific Ocean . The structure is located in the Cascadia region, off the west coast of North America , where tectonic plates are subjected to enormous forces.

The discovery, reported in a study published in Science Advances , shows that the oceanic plate subducting beneath North America has a much more complex structure than previously thought . The researchers have identified large fractures and zones with different seismic behaviors.

A fracture that cannot be seen from the surface

The crack is not a gigantic opening visible on the seafloor. It is a structure located within the plate , whose existence has been reconstructed using seismic exploration techniques and sound waves.

The scientists studied the oceanic subsurface using data obtained during research campaigns in Cascadia. The resulting images reveal that the Juan de Fuca plate and other associated structures are undergoing progressive fragmentation as they move toward the Earth's mantle. The extent of the fracture, close to 75 kilometers, makes this phenomenon an especially interesting piece for understanding how oceanic plates deform.

A clue to understanding earthquakes

The significance of the discovery goes far beyond the size of the fracture. Cascadia is a region under especially close watch for its tectonic activity and its ability to generate major earthquakes.

The new observations allow the direct study of processes that until now had to be reconstructed from ancient rocks and geological structures. Fractures can alter the way stresses are distributed within a plate and provide information about submarine seismic activity.

Researchers do not consider the finding to mean that a major earthquake is about to occur imminently. Its importance lies in providing a more precise picture of the evolution of the plates and of the mechanisms involved in their rupture.

The next step will be to continue monitoring this area to determine how the fractures evolve and what relationship they maintain with seismic activity. The Pacific seabed thus once again shows that, although it may seem motionless, beneath its waters the Earth is constantly undergoing enormous transformations.

articles.title: Andrew Carnegie, philanthropist and industrialist: "As I grow older, I pay less attention to what men say. I just watch what they do"
articles.standfirst: Andrew Carnegie's words about judging people by their actions reflect a philosophy that became increasingly important
articles.summary: Andrew Carnegie's words about judging people by their actions reflect a philosophy that became increasingly important
articles.body:
A ndrew Carnegie spent much of his life surrounded by ambitious people, powerful businessmen and political figures , but one of his most memorable observations placed greater importance on behavior than promises.

"As I grow older, I pay less attention to what men say. I just watch what they do"

The quotation, attributed to Carnegie , remains particularly relevant because his own life was defined by the contrast between words and action. He did not simply write about the responsibilities that came with wealth.

After becoming one of the richest men in the world, he devoted much of his later life to giving his fortune away and creating institutions intended to have an impact long after his death.

The Carnegie Hero Fund Commission also preserves the quote as part of its collection of Carnegie sayings.

Born in Dunfermline, Scotland, in 1835, Carnegie moved with his family to the United States when he was 12. His formal education ended at a young age, but access to books played an important role in his self-education.

After arriving in Pennsylvania , he worked in a cotton factory before moving through a series of jobs that eventually brought him into the railroad industry.

His career subsequently moved into steel, where he built Carnegie Steel into an enormous industrial enterprise.

In 1901, he sold the company to J.P. Morgan in a deal valued at $480 million, allowing him to retire from business and concentrate increasingly on philanthropy.

That transition is important when considering his famous observation. Carnegie had spent decades in an environment where results mattered.

Businesses could make ambitious claims about their future, but ultimately their success depended on production, investment and execution.

Carnegie turned his philosophy into action

His approach to philanthropy became especially clear through his belief that wealthy people had a responsibility to use their fortunes for the wider public good.

In his 1889 essay The Gospel of Wealth, Carnegie argued that wealthy individuals should regard themselves as trustees of their fortunes rather than simply accumulating money or passing it entirely to their heirs.

He advocated using wealth to support causes capable of creating lasting benefits for society.

Libraries became one of the clearest examples of that philosophy.

Carnegie had personally experienced the importance of having access to books when he was young.

Colonel James Anderson had opened his private library to working boys in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, giving Carnegie an opportunity to read at a time when he could not afford to purchase books himself. That experience helped shape his later commitment to public libraries.

Eventually, Carnegie and the philanthropic organizations associated with him helped fund 2,509 public libraries, including 1,681 in the United States. The projects were not simply monuments to Carnegie's wealth.

His funding generally came with the expectation that communities would take responsibility for operating and maintaining the libraries.

His philanthropy extended far beyond books. Carnegie supported educational institutions, scientific research, peace initiatives, museums and other civic projects.

In 1911, he established Carnegie Corporation of New York with a $135 million endowment, giving the organization a mission centered on the advancement and diffusion of knowledge and understanding.

Carnegie's legacy was therefore built not merely on the fortune he accumulated, but on what he ultimately did with it.

There is also an important nuance to his reputation. Carnegie's industrial career took place during the Gilded Age and his business practices, particularly the treatment of workers, remain part of the historical debate surrounding his legacy.

The Homestead Strike of 1892, in particular, became one of the defining labor conflicts associated with Carnegie Steel.

That makes his quotation about watching actions rather than listening to words especially interesting when viewed through a modern historical lens.

Carnegie's own legacy contains both his extraordinary rise in industry and the controversies surrounding the methods and conditions of that era.

Nevertheless, the practical message behind the quotation has endured. Promises can be persuasive, but sustained behavior provides a clearer indication of a person's priorities.

Carnegie himself left behind a complicated but remarkably visible example. His wealth helped make him one of the defining industrialists of his generation, while his decision to distribute much of that fortune transformed his name into one associated with libraries, education, culture and philanthropy.

More than a century after his death in 1919, the quotation continues to resonate because its central lesson is straightforward: people can describe their intentions in countless ways, but their choices ultimately provide the strongest evidence of what they truly value.

articles.title: Archaeologists believe they've found the remains of Noah's Ark in Turkey
articles.standfirst: The Durupinar formation has divided believers and geologists for decades, but new drilling is adding fresh evidence to the debate
articles.summary: The Durupinar formation has divided believers and geologists for decades, but new drilling is adding fresh evidence to the debate
articles.body:
The latest chapter in the search for Noah’s Ark is unfolding near Mount Ararat , where a research team says fresh core samples are challenging one of the most common explanations for the Durupinar formation.

The roughly 538-foot-long structure has been debated since it was identified in 1959, largely because of its boat-like outline and location in a region traditionally associated with the Genesis flood account.

Geologists have generally regarded Durupinar as a natural formation shaped by erosion, limestone and volcanic material. Researchers with Noah’s Ark Scans , however, say recent drilling has not produced the solid bedrock they expected critics to point to.

“In archaeology, you deal with probabilities, and we’re inching towards where we believe we will have confirmation this winter after our soil analysis is done,” project founder Andrew Jones said.

Core drilling becomes the focus

Jones said the group drilled at more than a dozen locations across the formation.

“They’ve criticized in the past, saying all those scans you can interpret different ways, ‘This is a solid mass of rock, a syncline or a block of bedrock,’” he said. “Well, we’ve core drilled… over 12 locations. We did not find bedrock at all.”

Instead, the researchers say they encountered deposits of rich, dark soil.

Those samples are expected to undergo laboratory analysis for organic material, which the team hopes could help determine whether the site contains traces consistent with decayed wood or past human activity.

“Noah’s Ark was a giant wooden boat, according to the Bible,” Jones said. “As wood decays, you’re gonna find elevated organic matter.”

He added that earlier testing in 2024 reportedly found around three times more organic material inside the formation than in samples taken outside it.

A site with decades of disputed claims

Durupinar has a long history of competing interpretations. Early investigations concluded there was no archaeological evidence proving the site was man-made.

Interest returned in the 1980s when salvage expert David Fasold used ground-penetrating radar and argued that the formation resembled the remains of a ship, though he later publicly rejected that conclusion.

The current team says more recent radar work has identified possible underground corridors and chambers, including one feature extending more than 250 feet.

Researchers ultimately hope to send a specially adapted underground robot into drilled spaces to capture footage and collect additional samples. The next major test will be the soil analysis.

Even elevated organic material wouldn't confirm Noah’s Ark , and natural processes could still explain what researchers find beneath the surface.

What the latest drilling does provide is another set of data points in a debate that has persisted for decades.

The question now is whether those samples strengthen the case for something unusual beneath Durupinar , or simply add another layer to one of archaeology’s most enduring controversies.

articles.title: Aristotle, Greek philosopher: "We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit"
articles.standfirst: The famous line captures a central idea in Aristotle’s philosophy, even though he did not write those exact words
articles.summary: The famous line captures a central idea in Aristotle’s philosophy, even though he did not write those exact words
articles.body:
Few philosophical ideas have become as closely associated with personal improvement as the statement: "We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit"

The quotation is commonly attributed to the ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle and is frequently used in discussions about discipline, achievement and self-improvement.

Its message is straightforward: extraordinary results rarely come from one spectacular moment. Instead, they emerge from the actions a person consistently chooses to take. There is, however, an important qualification surrounding the quotation.

Aristotle did not write this sentence in this exact form. The wording is generally considered a modern formulation of ideas found in his Nicomachean Ethics, particularly his discussion of virtue, character and habit.

The attribution is therefore better understood as a summary of Aristotle's philosophy rather than a direct quotation from his surviving works. That distinction does not make the underlying idea any less relevant.

Aristotle , who lived from 384 to 322 B.C., spent considerable time examining what it means to live well.

His ethical philosophy centered on eudaimonia, often translated as flourishing or living well, and he argued that a good life required more than simply understanding what was right. People had to repeatedly put those principles into practice.

In Book II of the Nicomachean Ethics, Aristotle argues that moral virtue develops through habit. People become courageous by performing courageous actions, just as they become temperate through temperate behavior.

That concept explains why the famous modern formulation has endured.

Why Aristotle’s idea still resonates today

The power of the quote comes from its challenge to the way people often think about excellence.

It is tempting to associate success with isolated moments: an athlete winning a championship, an artist producing a masterpiece, a student achieving a perfect grade or a business leader making a transformational decision.

Aristotle's philosophy suggests that these moments are only the visible results of a much longer process.

Excellence becomes part of someone's character when the behaviors that produce it become established patterns.

That idea also changes how failure can be viewed. One bad performance does not necessarily define a person, just as one impressive achievement does not automatically make someone excellent. What matters is the broader pattern of choices.

Aristotle's argument was more sophisticated than the modern motivational version of the quote might suggest.

He did not simply argue that repeating any behavior creates virtue. The actions themselves matter, as does the reasoning and character behind them. In his account, someone must learn to choose appropriate actions and develop the character required to perform them consistently.

This is also why Aristotle's concept of virtue differs from the idea of simply following a rigid routine.

He believed virtue involved finding an appropriate balance in emotions and actions, guided by practical judgment. Courage, for example, sits between extremes such as cowardice and recklessness.

The broader lesson is that habits can shape character, but good habits require judgment.

Aristotle also distinguished between knowing something and actually living according to that knowledge.

In the Nicomachean Ethics, he criticizes people who believe that studying philosophical ideas alone will make them good. For Aristotle , understanding virtue has limited value unless it translates into action. That makes the modern interpretation particularly powerful.

A person can understand the importance of discipline without being disciplined. Someone can know how to behave courageously without actually acting courageously when circumstances become difficult.

Knowledge provides a foundation, but repeated action helps turn that knowledge into character.

The quote's enduring appeal therefore comes from a principle that remains easy to recognize: what people repeatedly practice eventually becomes part of who they are.

Whether the goal is athletic excellence, professional success, stronger relationships or personal growth, the idea encourages attention to ordinary actions rather than waiting for extraordinary opportunities.

The precise wording may not belong to Aristotle, but the philosophy behind it does. More than two millennia after his death, his argument remains a reminder that excellence is rarely created in a single moment. It is developed through choices, repetition and the character those choices gradually build.

Aristotle's philosophy suggests that these moments are only the visible results of a much longer process.
Excellence becomes part of someone's character when the behaviors that produce it become established patterns.

That idea also changes how failure can be viewed. One bad performance does not necessarily define a person, just as one impressive achievement does not automatically make someone excellent. What matters is the broader pattern of choices.
Aristotle's argument was more sophisticated than the modern motivational version of the quote might suggest.

He did not simply argue that repeating any behavior creates virtue. The actions themselves matter, as does the reasoning and character behind them. In his account, someone must learn to choose appropriate actions and develop the character required to perform them consistently.
This is also why Aristotle's concept of virtue differs from the idea of simply following a rigid routine.
He believed virtue involved finding an appropriate balance in emotions and actions, guided by practical judgment. Courage, for example, sits between extremes such as cowardice and recklessness.
The broader lesson is that habits can shape character, but good habits require judgment.
Aristotle also distinguished between knowing something and actually living according to that knowledge.

In the Nicomachean Ethics, he criticizes people who believe that studying philosophical ideas alone will make them good. For Aristotle , understanding virtue has limited value unless it translates into action. That makes the modern interpretation particularly powerful.
A person can understand the importance of discipline without being disciplined. Someone can know how to behave courageously without actually acting courageously when circumstances become difficult.
Knowledge provides a foundation, but repeated action helps turn that knowledge into character.
The quote's enduring appeal therefore comes from a principle that remains easy to recognize: what people repeatedly practice eventually becomes part of who they are.

Whether the goal is athletic excellence, professional success, stronger relationships or personal growth, the idea encourages attention to ordinary actions rather than waiting for extraordinary opportunities.

The precise wording may not belong to Aristotle, but the philosophy behind it does. More than two millennia after his death, his argument remains a reminder that excellence is rarely created in a single moment. It is developed through choices, repetition and the character those choices gradually build.
