articles.title: In 1977, a giant wave struck a ship, causing 62 containers to fall into the sea; 27 years later, a fisherman recovered a toy shark and five million Lego pieces
articles.standfirst: These pieces keep appearing from time to time, floating in the sea
articles.summary: These pieces keep appearing from time to time, floating in the sea
articles.body:
When it comes to bizarre occurrences, human history is full of them. In August 2024, a fishing boat found its nets filled with Lego pieces. At first, the crew couldn’t fathom how this collection had ended up there. The answer, in fact, lay nearly 27 years in the past.

In 1997, a cargo ship lost more than 50,000 Lego pieces during a voyage. This means that these items have been floating in the sea for over 25 years. Furthermore, people still report finding these toys from time to time. The cause of this incident was a wave that tipped the ship more than 60 degrees.

A project has been established to identify all the recovered pieces.

This event took place on February 13, 1997, when the container ship Tokyo Express could not withstand the impact during its voyage from Rotterdam to New York. Specifically, the incident occurred off the coast of Cornwall. It is estimated that 62 containers fell into the sea and were never recovered. As it happens, much of the cargo was related to a nautical theme—which explains why the items have managed to persist over the years.

A subsequent tally revealed that approximately 97,500 scuba tanks, 4,200 black octopuses, life jackets, fins, harpoons, plastic seaweed, and 33,941 toy dragons had been lost, as detailed by Demotivatour. Most curiously, these Lego pieces did not end up in just this one area.

Toys from that ship have been recorded on beaches in Wales, Ireland, the Isle of Man, the Channel Islands, and even as far away as Norway. A project called "Lego Lost at Sea" was even established, where people can register any pieces they find.

articles.title: In the 1960s, the Soviet Union drained a sea to irrigate cotton crops; today, shrubs have been planted to prevent dust storms
articles.standfirst: One of the most profound environmental transformations of the 20th century
articles.summary: One of the most profound environmental transformations of the 20th century
articles.body:
In the 1960s, the world witnessed how human needs once again took precedence over those of nature. During those years, the Soviet Union chose to divert water from two rivers, the main tributaries of the Aral Sea , one of the largest inland lakes on the planet. The goal was simply to support the expansion of agriculture and irrigate cotton crops.

Before human intervention, the Aral Sea covered some 68,000 square kilometers and provided livelihoods for dozens of local fishermen. The growth of agriculture led the Soviet Union to set its sights on this inland lake. Consequently, it began diverting water from the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers.

The role of a shrub in the desert that formed in the Aral Sea

The entire volume of water from the Aral Sea came to be used to irrigate crops, primarily cotton. Over the years, the lake ended up paying the price: the amount of water that evaporated exceeded the amount that flowed in from the rivers. As a result, more than 90% of the lake’s surface area was completely lost, and the lake bed—covering some 60,000 square kilometers—was laid bare.

Decades later, this area became known as the Aralkum Desert, but another problem began to emerge: salts and residues from agricultural activity were swept up by dust storms and affected the soil, crops, and air quality itself. In response, they decided to plant saxaul (Haloxylon), a shrub that Uzbekistan uses to prevent these dust storms from stirring up those harmful particles. So far, 1.7 million hectares have been planted.

articles.title: How professional farters turned an embarrassing bodily function into show business
articles.standfirst: Humanity’s fascination with flatulence goes back thousands of years
articles.summary: Humanity’s fascination with flatulence goes back thousands of years
articles.body:
Long before viral videos, reality television and comedians competing to shock audiences, some entertainers built their careers around a talent that most people would rather keep private: passing gas.

Professional farters, sometimes known as flatulists or “fartists,” have been making audiences laugh for centuries. And while the subject might seem like the lowest form of comedy, history has some surprisingly distinguished examples of people who turned their digestive abilities into a living and, in at least one case, earned a property grant from an English king.

Humanity’s fascination with flatulence goes back thousands of years. A fart-related joke recorded around 1900 B.C. is often cited as the oldest known joke, demonstrating that bathroom humor has been entertaining people since ancient times. But there is a considerable difference between making a joke about gas and making gas the centerpiece of a paying performance.

Roland the Farter: A royal entertainer with his own manor

One of the strangest examples is Roland le Petour, better known as Roland the Farter, an English entertainer who lived during the 12th century. His unusual talent reportedly earned him a manor, a remarkable reward for a performer whose signature act involved little more than a jump, a whistle and a well-timed burst of flatulence.

Roland’s property was associated with a form of feudal service known as serjeanty, under which land could be granted in exchange for a particular duty to the Crown. According to accounts of his arrangement, he was expected to perform his distinctive routine before King Henry II every Christmas.

The required performance was described as “a jump, a whistle, and a fart.” In other words, Roland had to deliver a three-part comedy routine to maintain his royal privilege. The arrangement is a reminder that medieval entertainment could take some decidedly unconventional forms.

Court jesters and other performers entertained powerful patrons with music, jokes, acrobatics and physical comedy. Roland simply specialized in a skill that few people would have thought worthy of a royal reward. His success, however, apparently did not last forever. Later accounts suggest that Henry III , who succeeded Henry II, disapproved of the performance and revoked Roland’s property grant.

The story has circulated for centuries, although some details of the arrangement and its eventual termination remain difficult to establish with certainty. Still, Roland’s reputation endured. Long before anyone coined the modern term “influencer,” he had become memorable enough to earn a place in the history of professional flatulence.

Le Pétomane: The French performer who turned farting into an art

Centuries after Roland, another entertainer took the business of passing gas to an entirely different level. Joseph Pujol, a French performer known professionally as Le Pétomane, became a sensation in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. His stage name was a play on the French word pétomane, meaning someone who specializes in flatulence.

Unlike Roland, whose fame rested largely on historical accounts, Pujol performed before paying audiences and became a celebrated attraction in Paris. Pujol discovered that he could control the movement of air through his rectum and produce an extraordinary range of sounds. He initially demonstrated his ability to friends, who encouraged him to turn the unusual talent into a public act. He eventually reached the stage at the Moulin Rouge, one of Paris’ most famous entertainment venues.

There, he transformed what might have been a crude party trick into an elaborate comedy performance.

Pujol’s repertoire included imitations of different kinds of flatulence, from the timid sound attributed to a young girl to the nearly silent version associated with a bride on her wedding night. He also demonstrated his ability to extinguish candles with gas and, according to accounts of his act, smoke a cigarette using his anus.

For a finale, he would direct his flatulence through an ocarina, a small wind instrument, to perform musical numbers, including “O Sole Mio.”

The spectacle was more than a novelty. Audiences paid to see him, and his popularity made him one of the era’s most unusual stage celebrities. His success also helped establish flatulence as a form of theatrical entertainment at a time when variety shows and music halls thrived on eccentric performers.

Pujol’s act was so distinctive that it later inspired the character of Le Petomane in Mel Brooks’ 1974 Western comedy Blazing Saddles. The character’s appearance in the film introduced the name to a new generation of audiences, although the movie’s version was a comic adaptation rather than a documentary portrayal of Pujol’s life.

From royal courts to the Moulin Rouge

The careers of Roland and Pujol reveal an unlikely continuity in entertainment history: audiences have long been willing to pay for performers who can make them laugh through bodily functions. The circumstances, however, were very different.

Roland’s story belongs to a world in which royal favor could mean land, status and a livelihood. Pujol worked in a commercial entertainment industry where a performer’s success depended on selling tickets and attracting public attention.

Both men also benefited from the element of surprise. Flatulence is an everyday bodily function, but turning it into a controlled performance requires an unusual combination of timing, showmanship and, in Pujol’s case , remarkable physical control.

That does not mean every story about professional farters should be taken at face value. Historical anecdotes can become embellished as they are retold, and claims about earnings, audiences and royal arrangements sometimes outlive the evidence supporting them.

articles.title: The mysterious alien-looking creature unleashing terror in Ciudad Juárez: reality or fake?
articles.standfirst: A terrifying alert has shaken the residents of the Juárez Valley following the spread of alleged images of a being with an unknown appearance
articles.summary: A terrifying alert has shaken the residents of the Juárez Valley following the spread of alleged images of a being with an unknown appearance
articles.body:
Panic began to spread across the northern strip of Chihuahua בעקבות several incidents reported by residents of the area. According to reports and investigations published by international media such as the British newspaper The Sun, security cameras with motion sensors allegedly captured the strange beast , unleashing a wave of theories about its origin.

This phenomenon has once again sparked fascination with the unknown and stories about unidentified fauna in rural areas of the border . On social media and local forums, the debate has become polarized between those who claim it is a real threat to the community and those who believe it is just a viral hoax.

The released images show blurry figures that have reignited fear among ranchers in the region, concerned about the safety of their herds . Below, we review all the details surrounding this case, the images circulating, and the different explanations put forward to date.

A mysterious predator in the Juárez Valley

According to local testimonies collected during the recent inquiries, several residents reported the mysterious disappearance of hens, roosters, and rabbits from their pens . One of the accounts that raised alarm came from a local child, who claimed to have seen an animal grab a hen by the head before quickly climbing to the top of a tree.

After the first reports spread, Jaime Maussan's collaborators went to the site and installed trail cameras at key points. The photographic and infrared footage captured a quadrupedal specimen with light-colored fur, a long tail, and limbs with long fingers climbing a brick wall, l which made it possible to estimate that the animal measures close to 1.8 meters in length, including its 90-centimeter tail .

Although the recordings show the creature moving agilely on four legs, the case investigators claim that it would have the ability to stand upright and propel itself in large jumps . However, in the released footage it is not seen walking bipedally at any point.

Interdimensional beast or biological mutation?

The controversial statements raised in the Mexican and international press fueled the debate by suggesting that the specimen does not correspond to any mammal recorded in the area . Within ufological circles, some have even speculated that the being does not necessarily come from outer space, but rather could have crossed over to Earth from a parallel dimension given its unusual physiognomy and abilities .

On the other hand, biologists and wildlife specialists who have reviewed the case flatly rule out supernatural or extraterrestrial explanations. The leading scientific hypothesis suggests that it could be a local mammal with some genetic mutation or malformation , or simply a visual misidentification caused by common animals seen from unusual angles, such as raccoons, wild cats, or large rodents.

This type of sighting often evokes famous precedents from popular culture in Mexico, such as the legend of the Chupacabras or the Metepec Creature in the 1990s. In all of those historical cases, subsequent biological and genetic analyses ended up proving that they were known animals or elaborate hoaxes .

The authorities' stance and official skepticism

Despite the strong impact caused on social media and the concern of several local families, Ciudad Juárez Civil Protection agencies ruled out any kind of official alert . Municipal authorities clarified that there are no formal reports filed with the police nor confirmed complaints about creatures attacking livestock or threatening neighbors.

Likewise, border and institutional authorities in the state of Texas, on the other side of the U.S. border, confirmed that there are no records of attacks on animals or unusual sightings within their territory . Therefore, official agencies have asked the population to remain calm and avoid spreading unfounded rumors.

Independent experts and researchers call for caution regarding this type of news, recalling previous controversial episodes linked to Maussan , such as the presentation before the Congress of Mexico of alleged three-fingered mummies found in Peru, which subsequent scientific analyses identified as assemblages made with human and animal remains. For the time being, the presence of this creature in Juárez remains a viral phenomenon without proven biological basis .

articles.title: They filled 1,100 old tires with earth and built a 240 m² house: this is the sustainable home of this couple
articles.standfirst: Sarah Rowe and Gus Anning built a four-bedroom, three-bathroom home in New Zealand
articles.summary: Sarah Rowe and Gus Anning built a four-bedroom, three-bathroom home in New Zealand
articles.body:
C onstructing a family home by reusing more than a thousand used tires may seem like a far-fetched idea, but a couple from New Zealand has shown that it is possible to turn waste into a home. Sarah Rowe and Gus Anning built a 240-square-meter house in Hikuai, on the Coromandel Peninsula, with a structure that incorporates around 1,100 tires filled with earth. The result is a spacious home, with four bedrooms, three bathrooms, and open spaces, designed to reduce the environmental impact of construction.

The project was born after both of them explored different alternatives for building in a more sustainabl e way. The preparation took several years, while gathering the necessary tires required six months. Once the materials had been collected and the work organized, the couple managed to finish the home in nine months, with the help of several dozen volunteers who took part in the process.

Tires, earth, and reclaimed materials to build a bioclimatic house

The method used consists of placing the tires one on top of another and filling them with soil extracted from the site itself. Then, the walls are covered with a finishing layer that conceals the reused materials and provides a uniform surface. The couple also made use of earth bricks from another construction project to build interior partitions. Even the broken fragments were given a second life, by being crushed and mixed with other materials.

The home follows the principles of what are known as Earthships, constructions that seek to make use of natural resources and reduce dependence on conventional utilities. A large glazed facade makes it possible to capture solar radiation, while the windows and ventilation ducts help regulate the indoor temperature during the different seasons of the year.

Sustainability is also present in water management . The house has a system for collecting rainwater and features a covered terrace of almost 60 square meters. For cooking, its owners use gas cylinders. All of this is part of a strategy to reduce resource consumption and make the most of the characteristics of the surroundings.

The initiative demonstrates how materials that would normally end up in a landfill can be incorporated into alternative architectural projects. However, this type of construction requires careful planning and technical knowledge to ensure the safety, insulation, and durability of the home. In the case of Sarah and Gus, the combination of tires, earth, and other reclaimed elements has made it possible to shape a family home committed to reuse and bioclimatic design.

articles.title: Great white shark photobombs California beachgoers with a spectacular leap
articles.summary: A group of friends was posing for beach photos at Marina State Beach in California when a great white shark leaped out of the water in the background.
articles.body:
A group of friends was posing for beach photos at Marina State Beach in California when a great white shark leaped out of the water in the background.

The unexpected jump made it into the video, turning a casual photo moment into a startling wildlife sighting.

California State Parks confirmed a shark matching the great white’s characteristics was spotted off the beach around the time of the video. Shark notices are in effect at the beach.

articles.title: Pablo Neruda, writer: “Even if they cut all the flowers, they will not be able to stop spring”
articles.standfirst: The Chilean poet's most widely shared phrase hides a surprise about its authorship
articles.summary: The Chilean poet's most widely shared phrase hides a surprise about its authorship
articles.body:
T here are ideas that outlive those who formulate them. They pass from mouth to mouth, cross borders and generations, and end up becoming part of the common heritage, to the point that almost no one wonders where they came from.

Few phrases have traveled as far as this one. “They can cut all the flowers, but they cannot stop spring” is repeated on banners, murals, and social media, almost always attributed to Pablo Neruda . Its message is clear: the visible manifestations of something can be destroyed, but not the force that makes them sprout again and again .

That is why it has become a slogan of resistance. Movements all over the world have embraced it, and in Chile it reappeared strongly during the protests of 2019 .

However, there is a problem: there is no evidence that Neruda wrote it. His biographer, Mark Eisner , acknowledges that the quote is apocryphal , since it does not appear in any of his works nor is there any record that he ever said it. Nor could he have written it against Pinochet , as is often claimed: the poet died twelve days after the 1973 coup.

Even so, the fact that the phrase is attributed to him is no coincidence. Nature as a metaphor for life and political commitment run through much of his work.

Pablo Neruda, a Nobel announced on October 21

On October 21, 1971 , the Swedish Academy announced that Neruda was the winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature . The jury highlighted a poetry that, with the force of a natural element , gave life to the destiny and dreams of an entire continent. At that time, the author of Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair and Canto General was Chile’s ambassador to France.

He received the award in Stockholm in December. It was the second Nobel Prize in Literature for Chile , after the one Gabriela Mistral received in 1945, and the definitive recognition of one of the great voices in Spanish.

articles.title: Transatlantic Terror: Paris-Bound Air France Flight Declares Mid-Air Emergency, Diverts 500 Miles Short of Destination
articles.standfirst: They ended up landing in Dublin at dawn
articles.summary: They ended up landing in Dublin at dawn
articles.body:
C rossing the Atlantic Ocean on a transcontinental flight can become an odyssey if the weather does not cooperate. We all think that, according to modern civil aviation, no route or itinerary is at any risk, but nothing could be further from the truth if the problem is already inside the aircraft. This happened aboard Air France flight AF99, whose direct journey between Houston and Paris was disrupted in the middle of the night.

While the vast majority of the passengers were resting at an altitude of about 10,000 meters and the aircraft was approaching the European coast, alarms went off in the cockpit . One of the travelers began to suffer extremely serious health complications.

Faced with such a serious medical situation in the middle of the ocean, the crew did not hesitate: the priority stopped being the final destination and became saving that person's life. “It was, indeed, an ill passenger. Once the passenger was attended to by medical services on the ground, the flight was able to resume its course to Paris,” the airline said in a statement.

What did they do on Air France flight AF99 to handle this emergency?

The pilots issued transponder code 7700, an international signal warning air traffic control that the aircraft needs absolute priority to maneuver and land. Therefore, the Boeing 777-300ER headed for the nearest airport, regardless of the region

The commander diverted the planned route to the nearest safe point: Dublin Airport, located nearly 800 kilometers from Paris-Charles de Gaulle . The plane landed at dawn in the Irish capital, where medical teams were already waiting right on the runway to disembark and urgently transfer the patient.

Once attended to, the plane resumed its course and completed the final leg of the journey without any further setbacks.

The pilots issued transponder code 7700, an international signal warning air traffic control that the aircraft needs absolute priority to maneuver and land. Therefore, the Boeing 777-300ER headed for the nearest airport, regardless of the region

articles.title: Thrift Store Jackpot: $25 Charity Shop Purchase Turns Out to Be Rare Imperial Chinese Treasures Worth $74,000
articles.standfirst: The collector acquired the pieces without knowing their origin
articles.summary: The collector acquired the pieces without knowing their origin
articles.body:
Sometimes, the greatest treasures appear where they are least expected. That is what happened to a collector who found two colored vases in a charity shop in London. He paid around 20 pounds for both ($25) without imagining that those pieces would end up starring in an auction for an amount thousands of times higher than their original price.

The objects, which at first glance could have been mistaken for simple ornaments, caught his attention because of their characteristics and the marks on their base. After investigating their possible origin , he decided to turn to specialists to learn their true value. The result confirmed that they were not ordinary ceramics, but two pieces of 18th-century Chinese porcelain linked to the Qing dynasty.

Imperial marks that drove up their value

The two vessels, approximately 11.4 centimeters tall, stand out for their floral decoration. Against a yellow background, red and yellow chrysanthemums appear, accompanied by lotus flower motifs and green leaves. Their craftsmanship reflects the traditional Chinese doucai technique, which combines underglaze blue painting with other colors applied later.

The pieces were made in Jingdezhen, a town in China's Jiangxi Province historically known for its porcelain production. On their bases appear marks associated with Emperor Qianlong, who ruled between 1735 and 1796 and whose reign was closely linked to the arts and to the production of objects intended for the imperial court.

The pair went up for auction at Roseberys, a London house specializing in art and antiques, in May 2023. The sale reached £58,000, including the buyer's premium, a figure above $74,000. The result turned an apparently insignificant purchase into an extraordinary find.

Despite showing some defects, such as small cracks and scratches, the pieces aroused notable interest because of their age, their decoration, and their connection to Chinese imperial porcelain. The case demonstrates the extent to which the experience of specialists can be decisive in the antiques market: objects that go unnoticed in second-hand shops may conceal exceptional historical and economic value.

articles.title: They rescue a kangaroo in the middle of the sea three kilometers off the coast: "I had never seen anything like it in my life"
articles.standfirst: Some fishermen found it exhausted in Boston Bay, south of Australia
articles.summary: Some fishermen found it exhausted in Boston Bay, south of Australia
articles.body:
What was supposed to be a routine day of fishing ended up turning into an unusual rescue. The crew of a boat fishing in Boston Bay , off the town of Port Lincoln , in the state of South Australia , found a kangaroo swimming about three kilometers from the coast this week. The fishermen managed to pull it aboard and take it back to shore, according to the Australian public broadcaster ABC .

It was the boat's skipper , Ryan Smith , who raised the alarm after saying he had seen a kangaroo in the water. His companions did not believe him at first, but they decided to turn back to check. To their surprise , he was right: a male kangaroo was struggling to stay afloat in the middle of the bay.

To get it out of the sea , the crew opened the boat's side hatch , which is practically at water level. That allowed them to hold the animal underneath its front legs and hoist it aboard without too much trouble.

Hugging the kangaroo until reaching land

Jake Murray , a diver and farmer, is used to dealing with wild animals, but he had never experienced anything like this. During the trip back, he made sure to keep the kangaroo calm by hugging it and controlling its hind legs , which are especially strong. According to his account, the animal was exhausted and soaked after spending quite a while swimming, so much so that, while he was holding it, it seemed to be taking a little nap.

Among the crew was Miguel Villarroel, a diver from the Galápagos Islands who, despite having lived in Australia for some time, was seeing a kangaroo for the first time. When he asked whether that was something usual, Murray was blunt: “I had never seen anything like that in my life” . The fisherman explained that he has seen kangaroos in shallow waters or on beaches, but never in the middle of the bay.

Murray does not know how the animal ended up so far from the coast. He points out that the calm sea or the currents could have carried it away , although he also joked with another hypothesis: that it was a young specimen that jumped into the water to impress its companions after accepting a dare.

Already on dry land, the kangaroo rested for a while on the beach sand before regaining its strength and moving away in great leaps.

articles.title: Aristotle, Greek philosopher: "Knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom"
articles.standfirst: The famous saying about self-awareness continues to inspire people seeking personal growth
articles.summary: The famous saying about self-awareness continues to inspire people seeking personal growth
articles.body:
Understanding yourself is often presented as the first step toward making better decisions, building stronger relationships and discovering what truly matters in life.

The popular saying "Knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom" captures that idea in a single sentence, which is why it continues to circulate among readers interested in philosophy and personal development.

The words are widely attributed to Aristotle , the ancient Greek philosopher whose work shaped Western thinking about ethics, reason and human flourishing.

However, there is an important qualification: there is no reliable evidence that Aristotle wrote or spoke this exact sentence. The attribution is disputed, and the quotation does not appear in his surviving works. Aristotle did refer to the traditional expression "know thyself" in his Rhetoric, but that is different from endorsing the modern wording commonly shared online.

Even with that uncertainty, the idea behind the saying remains closely connected to questions Aristotle explored throughout his philosophical career.

Born in 384 BCE in Stagira, northern Greece, Aristotle studied under Plato in Athens before establishing his own school, the Lyceum. His writings covered subjects ranging from politics and biology to logic, human behaviour and morality.

Rather than treating wisdom as simply the possession of information, he examined how people could use reason to live better lives.

Why self-knowledge matters in everyday life

The appeal of the quotation lies in its suggestion that personal development begins with honest reflection. People can spend years pursuing professional success, recognition or financial security without examining whether those ambitions genuinely reflect their values.

Self-knowledge encourages a different approach. It involves recognizing personal strengths, acknowledging weaknesses and understanding how emotions influence decisions.

Someone who understands their tendency to react impulsively, for example, can learn to pause before responding to a difficult situation. A person who recognizes their own insecurities may become better equipped to accept criticism without interpreting every disagreement as a personal attack.

This process is not always comfortable. People naturally develop ideas about who they are, and those beliefs can become difficult to question.

Yet genuine self-awareness requires more than focusing on positive qualities. It also means accepting mistakes, identifying unhelpful habits and being willing to change.

Aristotle's ethical philosophy offers a useful perspective here. In the Nicomachean Ethics, he argued that living well involves developing virtues such as courage, justice and temperance.

These qualities are not simply acquired by reading about them; they are developed through habits, practice and repeated choices.

For Aristotle , understanding the good life was not merely an intellectual exercise. Ethical reflection was valuable because it could help people make better decisions and cultivate a more virtuous character.

From reflection to meaningful change

Knowing yourself is only useful if that awareness influences how you live. Recognizing a weakness, for instance, does not automatically overcome it. The next step is deciding what to do with that knowledge.

This is where reflection and action meet. Someone who realizes they struggle to maintain commitments might begin setting realistic goals rather than making ambitious promises they cannot keep.

Another person who recognizes that they depend too heavily on external approval may learn to make choices based more firmly on personal principles.

Aristotle's emphasis on habit is particularly relevant. Character develops through repeated actions, meaning that small, consistent decisions can gradually shape the kind of person someone becomes.

Courage, generosity and self-control are strengthened by practising them, not simply by admiring them as ideals.

Self-awareness also helps people understand their relationships. Recognizing how they communicate, respond to conflict and treat others can make it easier to build trust and acknowledge when they are wrong.

Wisdom, in this sense, is not about believing that you have all the answers. It is about remaining willing to learn.

The enduring lesson behind the famous quote

The quotation's popularity reflects a lasting human concern: how can people make meaningful progress if they do not understand themselves?

Although the precise wording should not confidently be presented as Aristotle's own, its central theme remains relevant to his broader philosophical approach.

His work encourages readers to consider their habits, examine what constitutes a good life and recognize the importance of practising virtue over time.

Self-knowledge does not guarantee happiness, nor does it eliminate uncertainty. People change, circumstances shift and even carefully considered decisions can produce unexpected outcomes. Understanding yourself is therefore an ongoing process rather than a destination.

The lasting value of the saying is its reminder that progress begins with reflection. Before deciding what to pursue, it helps to understand why a particular goal matters.

Before judging another person, it is worth examining your own assumptions. And before trying to change the world around you, there is value in looking honestly at your own behaviour.

Whether or not Aristotle ever expressed the idea in these exact words, the principle remains powerful: wisdom involves more than knowing facts. It also requires the willingness to understand yourself, question your choices and use what you learn to live more thoughtfully.

articles.title: Seneca, philosopher: "The whole future lies in uncertainty; live immediately"
articles.standfirst: The Roman philosopher believed constantly waiting for a better tomorrow could prevent people from appreciating the time they already have
articles.summary: The Roman philosopher believed constantly waiting for a better tomorrow could prevent people from appreciating the time they already have
articles.body:
People spend much of their lives preparing for what comes next. They work toward promotions, save for retirement, plan important milestones and convince themselves that happiness will arrive once their circumstances finally improve.

Yet Seneca , the Roman philosopher and one of the most influential figures in Stoicism, believed that constantly looking toward the future carried an overlooked danger: allowing the present to disappear without ever truly experiencing it.

His warning was captured in a remarkably direct statement: "The whole future lies in uncertainty: live immediately."

Written almost two millennia ago, the message challenges the assumption that life can safely be postponed until people achieve financial security, professional success or some imagined moment when everything falls into place.

Seneca expressed this idea in On the Shortness of Life, a philosophical work examining why people so often feel they have insufficient time.

His argument wasn't simply that human life is brief. Rather, he believed people frequently squander the time available to them by becoming consumed with obligations, ambitions and expectations.

In one passage, Seneca wrote: "The greatest obstacle to living is expectancy, which hangs upon tomorrow and loses today."

He was criticizing the tendency to treat the present as merely preparation for a future that nobody can guarantee.

That distinction is central to understanding his philosophy. Seneca was not suggesting that people should abandon responsibilities, reject long-term goals or behave recklessly.

Instead, he encouraged individuals to recognize that planning for tomorrow shouldn't come at the expense of living meaningfully today.

Waiting for happiness was a mistake

Seneca 's philosophy developed within the Stoic tradition, which emphasizes reason, self-discipline and recognizing the difference between circumstances people can influence and those beyond their control.

The future, by its nature, contains countless uncertainties. Careers can change unexpectedly, relationships evolve, and personal plans are vulnerable to events nobody can fully anticipate.

Allowing happiness to depend entirely on achieving particular outcomes therefore places personal fulfillment at the mercy of circumstances that may never materialize.

Seneca 's alternative was to place greater importance on how people spend their time now, including their relationships, responsibilities and personal development.

His argument also highlights the difference between productive ambition and endless postponement. Working toward something meaningful can enrich life, but continually delaying satisfaction until the next achievement risks creating an exhausting cycle.

Why Seneca's advice remains relevant 2,000 years later

Modern life offers countless opportunities to postpone personal fulfillment, particularly when professional demands and financial pressures make the future seem more important than the present.

People may delay reconnecting with loved ones, pursuing interests or making necessary changes because they believe a more convenient moment will eventually arrive.

Seneca 's warning encourages a different approach to recognize what matters and make room for it within the life already being lived.

This doesn't require dramatic decisions or abandoning sensible plans. Small actions, meaningful conversations and greater attention to everyday experiences can reflect the same principle.

The philosopher's enduring lesson is that preparing for the future has value, but time itself cannot be saved indefinitely.

Tomorrow may bring new opportunities, but today remains the only moment in which people can act.

articles.title: Albert Einstein, physicist: "Two things are infinite: the universe and human stupidity; and I'm not sure about the universe"
articles.standfirst: The sharp observation about human nature remains one of the most recognisable sayings associated with the celebrated physicist
articles.summary: The sharp observation about human nature remains one of the most recognisable sayings associated with the celebrated physicist
articles.body:
Few quotations attributed to Albert Einstein capture people's attention quite like the remark about the universe and human stupidity.

Its appeal lies in the contrast between one of science's greatest mysteries and a familiar source of frustration: the decisions people make, even when the evidence suggests they should know better.

The saying, “Two things are infinite: the universe and human stupidity; and I'm not sure about the universe”, has circulated for decades, appearing on quotation websites such as Goodreads and in collections of memorable observations.

Its humorous tone seems to fit Einstein's popular image as a brilliant scientist who could also offer an incisive perspective on everyday life.

Yet there is a complication behind the famous line. Although it is routinely credited to Einstein , researchers have not established a reliable contemporary record confirming that he actually said it.

The quotation's history is more complicated than its widespread attribution suggests, making it an interesting example of how memorable words can become attached to famous figures over time.

That uncertainty does not necessarily explain away the saying's popularity. Its message remains easy to understand, even for people who have little interest in physics.

The universe represents the vast unknown, while human stupidity represents the seemingly endless capacity to repeat mistakes, ignore evidence or act without considering the consequences.

A famous quote with a disputed history

The origins of the saying have been investigated by Quote Investigator, which examined the available historical references to establish how the wording developed.

One of the earliest versions identified appears in Frederick S. Perls's 1947 book Ego, Hunger, and Aggression: A Revision of Freud's Theory and Method. In that edition, Perls attributed a similar observation to a “great astronomer” rather than naming Einstein directly.

Decades later, Perls connected the remark to Einstein in his own writing. His 1969 book Gestalt Therapy Verbatim included a shorter version, while his 1972 work In and Out the Garbage Pail contained a longer formulation resembling the quotation familiar today.

Perls claimed to have spent an afternoon with Einstein , but the surviving evidence does not independently establish that the physicist made the remark.

The distinction matters because a quotation's popularity is not proof of its authenticity. Goodreads itself labels the saying as an attribution without a source, despite listing Einstein as the author.

The available historical record therefore supports treating the words as a famous saying associated with Einstein , rather than a verified statement from him.

Why the observation still resonates

Part of the quotation's staying power comes from its ability to describe everyday experiences in just a few words.

People encounter misinformation, impulsive decisions and stubborn disagreements in public life, workplaces and personal relationships. The saying offers a humorous way to express frustration with behaviour that appears to defy common sense.

Its reference to the universe also gives the line a particularly effective contrast. Einstein devoted much of his professional life to understanding the physical world, including the relationship between space, time, gravity and energy. The Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to him for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, work that helped establish the foundations of quantum theory.

His scientific achievements make the quotation's contrast especially memorable, even if the attribution remains uncertain.

The cosmos presents questions that can take generations of scientific work to investigate, while human behaviour can sometimes seem inexplicable for much more ordinary reasons.

There is also a broader lesson in the remark. Intelligence and knowledge do not automatically prevent people from making poor decisions.

Recognising mistakes, questioning assumptions and listening to evidence are essential if individuals and societies are to learn from experience.

Ultimately, the quote endures because it combines humour with a recognisable truth about human nature. Its precise author may remain uncertain, but its popularity demonstrates how a short, witty observation can survive for generations.

And while scientists continue investigating the scale and nature of the universe, the saying invites readers to reflect on a different mystery: why people sometimes persist in doing things they know are unwise.

articles.title: Zhuangzi, Chinese philosopher: "Rewards and punishment are the lowest form of education"
articles.standfirst: The ancient Chinese thinker's philosophy challenges the idea that people learn best through prizes and penalties, arguing instead for a deeper understanding that comes from within
articles.summary: The ancient Chinese thinker's philosophy challenges the idea that people learn best through prizes and penalties, arguing instead for a deeper understanding that comes from within
articles.body:
The way people are taught can shape not only what they learn, but also why they choose to learn it.

A student might work hard to earn high marks, an employee may chase a bonus, and a child could follow the rules simply to avoid being punished. But what happens when the rewards disappear or nobody is left to enforce the rules?

A quote commonly attributed to the ancient Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi offers a thought-provoking answer: "Rewards and punishment are the lowest form of education".

The statement questions an approach to learning that depends heavily on external pressure rather than genuine curiosity or personal understanding.

Instead of encouraging people to explore ideas for themselves, rewards and penalties can turn education into a transaction in which the main objective is to gain something or avoid an unpleasant consequence.

Zhuangzi , also known as Chuang Tzu, was a central figure in classical Daoist philosophy who lived during China's Warring States period, around the fourth century BCE.

His teachings challenged conventional assumptions about how people should live, think and behave, often using imaginative stories and philosophical puzzles to question established ideas.

His approach placed considerable importance on living naturally and responding to the world without becoming overly constrained by artificial expectations.

In this context, the criticism of rewards and punishment reflects a broader concern about the limits of trying to control people from the outside.

There is, however, a distinction worth making about the quotation itself. Although the wording is widely circulated under Zhuangzi's name, the precise English phrase is not necessarily a direct, verifiable translation of a specific passage from the original text.

A quotation reference traces similar wording to Lionel Giles' 1906 translation and selection of Zhuangzi's writings, illustrating how translated philosophical sayings can evolve over time.

Why rewards and punishment can undermine the desire to learn

The idea behind the quotation has a striking connection with modern research into human motivation.

Psychologists distinguish between intrinsic motivation, in which people undertake an activity because they find it interesting or meaningful, and extrinsic motivation, in which they act to obtain an external benefit or avoid a negative consequence.

Neither form of motivation is automatically good or bad. A qualification can open career opportunities, while clear rules can help maintain a safe and productive learning environment.

The difficulty arises when external incentives become the main reason for doing something.

A major meta-analysis published in Psychological Bulletin in 1999 examined 128 studies on external rewards and intrinsic motivation.

Researchers Edward Deci, Richard Koestner and Richard Ryan found that certain expected, tangible rewards tied to participation, completion or performance could reduce people's intrinsic motivation. Their findings also indicated that positive feedback could support interest rather than undermine it.

The implications for education are significant. When students focus exclusively on grades, they may concentrate on memorising information for an examination instead of developing a lasting understanding of the subject. Once the assessment is over, the incentive to revisit the material can disappear.

Punishment can create a similar problem from the opposite direction. A student who fears detention or embarrassment might comply with classroom expectations without understanding why those expectations matter.

The behaviour may change temporarily, but the underlying attitude does not necessarily follow.

Research published in Perspectives on Psychological Science in 2021, analysing 344 samples involving more than 223,000 participants, also found that intrinsic motivation was associated with student success and well-being.

Motivation driven by rewards or avoiding punishment was not associated with performance or persistence in the same way and was linked to lower well-being.

Zhuangzi's philosophical perspective therefore invites a different question: rather than asking how to make someone obey, how can we help them understand the value of what they are doing?

That does not mean eliminating discipline, expectations or accountability. Children need boundaries, students require guidance, and institutions must maintain standards. Instead, the lesson is about ensuring those measures do not become substitutes for genuine learning.

Teachers can encourage curiosity by giving students opportunities to ask questions, explore different solutions and understand the reasons behind what they are studying.

Parents can praise persistence and effort rather than making approval dependent entirely on achievement. Employers can offer constructive feedback and opportunities for development instead of relying solely on financial incentives.

Ultimately, the quotation's enduring appeal lies in its challenge to the assumption that external control is the best way to encourage lasting change.

Rewards can offer short-term encouragement, and punishment can discourage unwanted behaviour, but neither guarantees that a person will develop independent judgment or a genuine interest in learning.

The deeper message is that education should help people become capable of directing themselves, rather than simply teaching them to respond to whoever holds the power to reward or punish them.

articles.title: Apophis will pass just 31,900 kilometers from Earth in April 2029: is there a risk of collision?
articles.standfirst: A distance shorter than the one separating our planet from the satellites orbiting it
articles.summary: A distance shorter than the one separating our planet from the satellites orbiting it
articles.body:
T he asteroid Apophis is one of those that causes the most intrigue and excitement among astronomers and lovers of the universe. Well, in April 2029, this rocky object about 340 meters in diameter , that is, three football fields, will pass approximately 31,900 kilometers from the Earth 's surface .

Apophis's pass in 2029 will allow scientists to study an asteroid of this size up close . In addition, if conditions allow, it will be possible to observe it from various points around the world , including Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia, and eastern South America.

This is how Apophis will pass close to our planet in April 2029

Undoubtedly, it is unthinkable to ask ourselves whether there is any risk in this regard. Experts make it clear: there is no reason to be alarmed, since they rule out Apophis colliding with our planet during this approach. Furthermore, according to recent calculations, it also does not pose a collision risk for at least the next 100 years.

Its passage will be of vital importance to understand how an asteroid of these dimensions behaves and acts when it comes so close to our planet . This is because Earth's gravity could slightly change its trajectory and physical characteristics, making it a unique opportunity to expand our knowledge about these objects.

Finally, this close approach in the year 2029 will also be monitored by various space missions . Among them, RAMSES, from the European Space Agency (EA), stands out, and its objective will be to study Apophis during this period, while NASA plans to use the mission OSIRIS-APEX to obtain information about Apophis’s composition and its properties.

In this way, the data collected will help to better understand the nature of near-Earth asteroids and their evolution.
